items.title: Theodore Purnell Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: I used to even have to lend him a horn to go play with. Cyril August.

ctx.x: That's lucky you got through depression like that. I used to, I used to halfway take care of one, one, one, great little now, something else we had. We never met season there. Yeah. We never, we never met season there. I used to even have to lend him a horn to go play with. Cyril August. That's right. That's right. He was good too, man. He had to lend him a horn to go play with. What's his name again? Cyril August.

Man, he's so... He was good. Yeah. He was there. He was real. Is he still around? No, he did. He was good. One of my tenders, he poured it and I was fixing to grab him but I looked at his wife and the kids and said, you know, mine. And he said, how do you know I had to get something for these kids? I said, sir, but you know, I'll let you go away from my place. I was waiting at the cotton club on Jefferson Highway. I said, I'll let you go away from my place.
